deduced_preparation_edges.mechanism: Investment products, risk-return language and financial news provide vocabulary for portfolio analysis.
Covariance matrices, quadratic forms and constrained optimization provide a mathematical way to understand portfolio risk and asset weights.
Probability, random processes and option-pricing foundations prepare for Brownian motion and Ito calculus.
deduced_preparation_edges.warning: Current EF3520 HTML has malformed prerequisite parentheses. Do not reconstruct a compulsory rule from it.

deduced_preparation_edges.mechanism: PDEs and numerical approximation help explain differential-equation pricing and computational schemes; EF4820 explicitly discusses PDE, binomial and Monte Carlo methods.
Applied statistical modelling can help with financial return series and empirical risk analysis; finance-specific inference still has to be learned.
Linear algebra represents data and parameters, optimization fits a model, and probability supports uncertainty and generalization reasoning.
AI applications, limitations and ethics motivate later algorithmic study; introductory GE does not supply programming competence.
Formal logic can help evaluate arguments, but creative thinking, cognitive biases and ethical reasoning remain separate demands.
